facts.label: Conflicts and comparability breaks
facts.text: 1. Product-category restatement. The latest 10-Q reclassified categories and restated the comparative quarter [10-Q-Sep26 page:9 — "Prior period amounts have been reclassified to conform to the current period presentation."]. The bridge shows the prior presentation and the effect [10-Q-Sep26 page:9 — "Cybersecurity (Enterprise) 180,747 (71,410) 109,337"]. Earlier filings and releases therefore show product-category revenue on the old basis. Both bases are retained; neither controls the other. Downstream effect: product-category trends across PR-May26, PR-Aug26 and the latest quarter are not comparable without the bridge, and the bridge covers only the Q1 FY2026 quarter. 2. Net leverage. The only stated ratio is a management statement [PR-Nov26 page:3 — "Our net leverage ratio is 2.55x as of September 30, 2026."]. The covenant is defined differently in the filing (total debt less unrestricted cash, including guarantees and letters of credit, over trailing-twelve-month adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, restructuring, share-based compensation and other charges). The release does not state its definition or inputs. This is a definitional gap rather than a numerical conflict; it must not be presented as the covenant ratio. A management claim does not override the filing, which states only compliance. 3. Debt at the cutoff versus debt at period end. The balance sheet debt is as of September 30, 2026, while the same report records an October 2026 refinancing: [10-Q-Sep26 page:43 — "On October 1, 2026, the Company issued $500 million in aggregate principal amount of 6.70% senior secured notes due 2031"] and [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "On October 2, 2026, the Company purchased and cancelled $300.0 million of the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the Senior Notes 2028"]. The contractual-obligation table states it excludes these events [10-Q-Sep26 page:84 — "The information presented herein does not give effect to the issuance of the Senior Secured Notes 2031"]. The release states the same events [PR-Nov26 page:3 — "In October, OpenText completed a $1.0 billion senior secured notes offering"]. The documents are consistent with each other; the consequence is that two debt registers (period end and pro forma for the subsequent events) are needed and must be labelled. 4. Revolver maturity. The period-end filing describes the revolver as maturing in December 2028 and then records an amendment on October 1, 2026 extending it, subject to conditions [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "extend its maturity from December 19, 2028 to October 1, 2031, subject to certain conditions"]. Both are retained as dated facts. 5. Rounding. Release headlines are in millions and release tables in thousands; the filings are in thousands. Differences of that kind are rounding, not conflicts.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: For OPEN TEXT CORP the financial base shows a credit that has de-levered and cut interest cost while its top line contracts. Gross debt principal at June 30, 2026 was below June 30, 2025 by the amount of repayments in FY2026, funded by divestiture proceeds and cash on hand, and debt at September 30, 2026 was almost unchanged from June 30, 2026. Against adjusted EBITDA, total debt fell from 3.63x at FY2025 to 3.07x at FY2026 and was 3.10x on a last-twelve-months basis at September 30, 2026; EBITDA to cash interest paid rose from 3.69x in FY2024 to 5.92x in FY2026 and 6.26x on the last-twelve-months basis. The calculated covenant ratio printed in the filings fell from 3.35 at December 31, 2025 to 2.75 at June 30, 2026 against a 4.50 maximum, so maintenance headroom is large on the printed figures. The pressure points are the contracting revenue base (Q1 FY2027 revenue down year on year, with client support and license lines falling while cloud grew), the divestitures that removed earnings together with debt, the heavy shareholder distributions in FY2026 relative to free cash flow, an unquantified Canada Revenue Agency tax dispute, and the October 2026 refinancing that lengthened maturities but swapped 6.90% secured notes due 2027 for 6.70% and 7.15% secured notes due 2031 and 2033, raising the secured debt share. The view is bounded by three missing inputs: covenant EBITDA, letters of credit that may reduce revolver availability, and cash after the October 2026 transactions.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: For OPEN TEXT CORP the business is a diversified, global enterprise software and cybersecurity vendor whose revenue is dominated by annual-renewal client support and cloud subscriptions, which gives good revenue visibility but a base that fell in the latest quarter, with the support and license lines declining and growth concentrated in cloud lines. The registrant is a widely held listed company with no sponsor and no holder above about eleven percent, so the creditor risk is not sponsor extraction; it is a management and Board capital allocation choice between debt reduction, a quarterly dividend and share repurchases, taken in a year of leadership change and a strategic enterprise assessment whose conclusions are scheduled for an investor day in February 2027. The credit-relevant history is acquisition-led: the 2023 Micro Focus acquisition created the debt load, the 2024 AMC sale and the 2026 eDOCS and Vertica sales repaid part of it at the cost of earnings, and the October 2026 refinancing replaced the 2027 secured notes and part of the 2028 notes with secured notes due 2031 and 2033, which extends the maturity wall but raises the share of secured debt and the coupon on the replaced paper. Management's FY2027 outlook, a management statement, points to a lower margin and lower free cash flow than the last twelve months, which is the main forward uncertainty. Evidence is primary and dated for facts and management-only for outlook and strategy; no customer-level, rating or executed-document evidence is available.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The transaction that matters for the creditor is the October 2026 refinancing, a closed subsequent event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and inside the cutoff. Type: a refinancing and partial liability management. Parties: the registrant as issuer, guaranteed on a senior secured basis by certain subsidiaries; the initial purchasers, trustees and holders tendering are not named in the pack. Sponsor: none. On October 1, 2026 the company issued two series of senior secured notes: [10-Q-Sep26 page:43 — "On October 1, 2026, the Company issued $500 million in aggregate principal amount of 6.70% senior secured notes due 2031"] and a second 500 million series at 7.15 percent due 2033, both paying interest semi-annually from April 15, 2027 and maturing on October 15, 2031 and October 15, 2033 respectively. Debt raised is therefore 1,000 million of new secured notes, secured with the same priority as the senior credit facilities [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "are secured with the same priority as the Company’s senior credit facilities"] and structurally subordinated to liabilities of subsidiaries that do not guarantee them. Use of proceeds: on October 2, 2026 the proceeds, together with cash on hand, funded the redemption in full of the 1.0 billion 6.90 percent senior secured notes due 2027 including the redemption premium, accrued interest and costs, and the cash purchase and cancellation of 300.0 million of the 3.875 percent senior notes due 2028 [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "On October 2, 2026, the Company purchased and cancelled $300.0 million of the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the Senior Notes 2028"]. The revolving credit facility of 750.0 million, undrawn at September 30, 2026, was amended on October 1, 2026 to extend its maturity from December 19, 2028 to October 1, 2031, subject to certain conditions, and its borrowings rank pari passu with the term loan and the new secured notes.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Effect on the credit, as the financial base handoff computes it: principal debt falls from 5,827,563 to 5,527,563 (US$ thousands); the nearest note maturity moves from December 1, 2027 to February 15, 2028 and falls from 1,900,000 across the two near notes to 600,000 for the remaining 2028 notes; new maturities of 500,000 fall in fiscal 2032 and 500,000 in fiscal 2034; secured principal stays at 2,527,563 while its share of the total rises from 43.4 percent to 45.7 percent; and the annual cash coupon on the exchanged notes falls by 11,375 before premium and fees. The cost side is not quantified in the pack: the redemption premium, the tender price and the cash used are not stated, so the liquidity effect is a reduction of cash on hand by an amount that is not supplied. The management characterisation is that the transactions provide greater financial flexibility [PR-Nov26 page:1 — "providing the Company with greater financial flexibility"], which is Management Language and is not adopted; the documented facts are a longer maturity profile, a higher secured share and coupons of 6.70 and 7.15 percent against 6.90 percent on the retired secured notes. Status: closed. New debt issues in the pack: only these two series; there are no pending or committed financings, no acquisition financing and no dividend recapitalisation.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Earlier transactions that shape the structure: the 2023 Micro Focus acquisition for 6.2 billion, for which the term loan and the 2027 secured notes were raised; the 2024 AMC sale for 2.275 billion, which funded a term loan prepayment of 1.31 billion in FY2024 together with cash on hand; and the eDOCS and Vertica sales in FY2026 for 163.0 million and 150.0 million, each applied to prepay the term loan. These sales removed revenue and earnings while reducing debt, which is why the divestiture comparability break is carried in every period comparison. A further dividend of $0.28 per share was declared on November 3, 2026, payable December 18, 2026; it is a future term, not an executed payment.

facts.label: Ownership, control and capital allocation
facts.text: Ownership is dispersed and institutional: the largest holder is just over eleven percent and directors and executive officers hold about two and a half percent. No sponsor, no prior sponsor ownership and no dividend recapitalisation history appears in the pack; none of the ownership percentages is inferred beyond the table. Capital allocation is documented: the company declares a quarterly non-cumulative dividend (dividends declared of $1.00, $1.05 and $1.10 per share in FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 per the equity statement [10-K page:236 — "Dividends declared ($1.10 per Common Share)"]) and runs a repurchase programme renewed in August 2026 [10-Q-Sep26 page:82 — "the Company renewed its share repurchase plan"]. The financial base handoff shows that shareholder distributions in FY2026 were 91.4 percent of free cash flow, in the same year that debt principal fell by 648,850. The dividend is subject to contractual limits [10-K page:67 — "Our dividend payments are subject to relevant contractual limitations, including those in our existing credit agreements"], whose terms are not in the pack, so legal capacity for distributions cannot be measured here.

facts.label: Conflicts
facts.text: 1. Term loan size in the annual report. A risk factor says [10-K page:61 — "our credit facilities consisted of a $2.23 billion Acquisition Term Loan and a $750 million committed revolving credit facility"] while the debt note at the same date shows [10-K page:268 — "Acquisition Term Loan 1,536,525 2,185,375"]. Both are retained and neither is reconciled here. The financial statement note is the filed financial authority for the balance at June 30, 2026, so the debt register uses the note; the risk factor figure is unexplained in the pack. Effect: the size of the term loan should be taken only from the notes and balance sheet. 2. eDOCS product category. The annual report places the business in one category [10-K page:19 — "eDOCS business (eDOCS), a part of our Analytics product category"] while the latest quarterly report places it in another [10-Q-Sep26 page:52 — "an on-premise solution (eDOCS), a part of its Portfolio product category"]. The latest report explains that prior amounts were reclassified [10-Q-Sep26 page:9 — "Historical revenues related to the eDOCS business, which was divested in Fiscal 2026, and previously included in Analytics, were reclassified to the Portfolio product category."]. Both versions are retained; the later basis applies to Q1 FY2027 and its comparative only. Effect: category trends across filings are not comparable.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: OPEN TEXT CORP is a moderately leveraged, cash-generative software credit whose balance sheet has improved, but whose revenue base is shrinking, so the credit view is stable-to-cautious rather than improving. The strongest support is deleveraging to 3.10x total debt to adjusted EBITDA on a last-twelve-months basis, cash interest cover of 6.26x, USD 844,805 thousand of last-twelve-months free cash flow, an 84.1 percent recurring revenue share and no sponsor. The weakest point is Q1 FY2027 revenue down 4.0 percent with support and license declining, while management guides to a lower margin and lower free cash flow than the last twelve months. What decides the outcome is whether cloud growth and cost actions hold earnings near USD 1,878,183 thousand against the guided USD 1,643.2 to 1,711.1 million, and whether distributions to shareholders are trimmed to keep paying debt down. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

facts.text: OPEN TEXT CORP has de-levered through divestiture proceeds and cash: debt principal fell from USD 6,485,375 thousand at June 30, 2025 to USD 5,836,525 thousand at June 30, 2026 and USD 5,827,563 thousand at September 30, 2026, taking total debt to adjusted EBITDA from 3.63x to 3.07x and then 3.10x on a last-twelve-months basis, and net debt to 2.58x [financial base]. Documentary Fact. The mechanism matters: part of the repayment came from selling businesses that also carried earnings, so the ratio improvement is real but partly bought with a smaller EBITDA base [business context timeline].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The interest burden has fallen sharply, from cash interest paid of USD 533,866 thousand in FY2024 to USD 300,111 thousand on a last-twelve-months basis, lifting adjusted EBITDA to cash interest from 3.69x to 6.26x [financial base]. Documentary Fact. Lower interest leaves more of each dollar of EBITDA to reach free cash flow, which was USD 844,805 thousand on a last-twelve-months basis, and gives earnings room to fall before debt service is strained. The cover uses issuer-defined adjusted EBITDA, which adds back share-based compensation and special charges that have recurred in each of the last three years (USD 135,305 thousand in FY2024, USD 145,890 thousand in FY2025 and USD 133,020 thousand in FY2026) [financial base], so cover on a stricter definition would be lower. Analyst Interpretation.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The covenant position is wide on the printed values: the calculated net leverage ratio was 3.35, 3.02 and 2.75 at December 2025, March 2026 and June 2026 against a maximum of 4.50 [financial base]. Documentary Fact. The September 30, 2026 value is not printed in the filing; management states 2.55x without a definition, and that statement stays attributed [financial base]. Management Language. Headroom of 1.75 turns at June 2026 means a maintenance breach is unlikely to be the first point of stress; the likelier constraint is cash flow used for distributions.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Recurring revenue gives visibility but the trend is negative: recurring revenue is 84.1 percent of Q1 FY2027 revenue, support revenue fell 9.0 percent and license 8.0 percent, while cloud grew 4.3 percent, and the cloud net renewal rate eased to 95 percent from 96 percent [business context]. Documentary Fact. Support is the largest revenue line and is annual-renewal, so attrition hits the highest-margin contracted base first; cloud growth is replacing it at a lower margin. Total revenue was down 4.0 percent year on year in Q1 FY2027 [financial base], partly from the eDOCS and Vertica sales.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The October 2026 refinancing extended the maturity profile but made the structure more secured. USD 500 million of 6.70 percent secured notes due 2031 and USD 500 million of 7.15 percent secured notes due 2033 replaced the USD 1,000 million 6.90 percent secured notes due 2027, USD 300 million of the 2028 notes were bought back and the USD 750.0 million revolver was extended to October 2031 [financial base; business context]. Documentary Fact. The nearest note maturity moves to February 2028 (USD 600.0 million), but the secured share of principal rises from 43.4 percent to 45.7 percent because unsecured notes were retired, so unsecured creditors rank behind a larger secured pool, while the annual cash coupon on the exchanged notes falls by USD 11,375 thousand. Cash used for the tender, the premium and costs are not supplied, so post-October liquidity is lower than the USD 983.3 million of cash at September 30, 2026 by an amount that cannot be stated.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. (1) Deleveraging and cover: total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 3.10x and cash interest cover of 6.26x on a last-twelve-months basis give room for earnings to fall; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact. (2) Recurring revenue and diversification: an 84.1 percent recurring share, no customer above 10 percent of receivables, no country other than the United States above 10 percent of revenue and a single reported segment spread across product categories reduce concentration; basis: business context. Documentary Fact. (3) Liquidity and maturities: USD 983.3 million of cash plus an undrawn USD 750.0 million revolver at September 30, 2026, before any letters of credit, a revolver extended to October 2031 and no note maturing before February 2028; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact. (4) Cash generation: USD 844,805 thousand of last-twelve-months free cash flow, up in Q1 FY2027 to USD 138,517 thousand from USD 101,229 thousand; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact. (5) Ownership: dispersed institutional holders and no sponsor remove the sponsor-extraction mechanic; basis: business context. Documentary Fact. (6) Covenant headroom of 1.75 turns at June 2026 on the printed ratio; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. (1) Shrinking base: revenue down 4.0 percent in Q1 FY2027, support down 9.0 percent, license down 8.0 percent, cloud net renewal rate down to 95 percent; basis: financial base and business context. Documentary Fact. (2) Guided step-down: the FY2027 outlook implies lower adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow than the last twelve months; basis: business context. Management Language, qualified. (3) Earnings quality: adjusted EBITDA relies on add-backs, including special charges that recur every year; basis: financial base. Analyst Interpretation. (4) Distribution intensity: 91.4 percent of FY2026 free cash flow returned to shareholders, leaving debt reduction that in FY2026 was partly funded by divestiture proceeds; basis: financial base. Analyst Interpretation. (5) Structure and cost: a larger secured share and higher coupons on the replacement notes; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact. (6) Contingent and unmeasured claims: the Canada Revenue Agency matter, which the filing sizes at approximately USD 88.8 million for fiscal 2012 to 2016 and up to approximately USD 470 million of deferred tax assets for fiscal 2017 to 2021 with no accrual, sits outside debt; letters of credit, guarantor structure, ratings and post-October cash are not supplied; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact for the amounts; Insufficient Information for the unmeasured items. (7) Leadership and strategy in flux: the chief executive and chief financial officer both changed within FY2026 and an enterprise assessment may change portfolio and reporting; basis: business context. Documentary Fact.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Illustrative leverage if the FY2027 outlook is met, with principal unchanged: pro forma principal USD 5,527.563 million divided by outlook-implied adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,711.1 million is 3.23x; divided by USD 1,643.2 million is 3.36x. Inputs from the financial base (principal 5,527,563 thousand) and the business context (outlook-implied EBITDA range 1,643.2 to 1,711.1 million). This ignores scheduled amortization and any further repayment, and uses gross principal because post-October cash is not supplied; it is a scenario, not a forecast. 2. Free cash flow after an annualized dividend at the Q1 FY2027 rate: dividends of USD 66.5 million in Q1 FY2027 times four is USD 266.0 million, which is 42.6 percent of the low end (USD 625 million) and 36.7 percent of the high end (USD 725 million) of guided free cash flow. Inputs: business context outlook range; dividend paid in Q1 FY2027 as stated in the financial base. Illustrative only; repurchases are excluded and discretionary. 3. All other figures (leverage, cover, margins, free cash flow, secured share of 45.7 percent, distributions of 91.4 percent, headroom of 1.75 turns) are taken without recalculation from the financial base and business context handoffs.

spans.text: ## Request

Module CP-0, source readiness, for OPEN TEXT CORP (issuer id otex; registrant Open Text Corporation, Canada, NASDAQ and TSX ticker OTEX). As-of date and evidence cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency per the run context: USD. Current period per the run context: Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended September 30, 2026); prior period: FY2026 (year ended June 30, 2026). The fiscal year ends June 30.

The question answered here is whether the pinned source set can support the requested downstream modules (CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5) and what remains blocked or limited. This module gives no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation and no investment opinion, and it does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. It assesses source sufficiency only; completion of downstream analysis is separate.

The run context (`context`) holds dated user settings. It contains no deal terms, quotes, ratings, peers, sponsor, borrower, parent or guarantor entries, and states legal documents as none. Blank context fields are treated as not supplied, not as zero.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on

Alias is used only for citations below. The hash is the sha256 of the extracted text file named in the first column. Each file is a page-chunked text extraction of the filed HTML document ("page:N" is the extracted chunk, not the printed page).

### Supplied handoffs
None. CP-0 is the first module of this run, so no upstream handoff exists to list. The pack also contains a retrieval index (`_retrieval.json`) that CP-OS ignored; it was not used as evidence.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven issuer documents are complete, current to the cutoff and sufficient for the four requested downstream modules, each of which can proceed with stated limitations. | Medium | No executed debt documents, ratings, letters-of-credit detail or guarantor financials were supplied, and the covenant ratio value is not printed in any filing. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The latest quarterly report was filed on the cutoff date and describes an October 2026 refinancing after quarter end. | Period-end debt differs from the debt outstanding at the cutoff, so the two must be shown separately. | High |
| The only net leverage figure is a management statement in the latest earnings release. | It cannot be tied to the covenant definition, so covenant headroom cannot be taken from filings. | Medium |
| Product categories were reclassified in the latest quarter, and two businesses were sold during FY2026. | Revenue trends across periods need care about comparability. | High |
| No ratings, letters-of-credit amounts or guarantor financial information were supplied. | Facility availability and the structural position of lenders cannot be fully assessed. | High |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is sufficient for CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 to run, each as READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, and nothing is BLOCKED or CONDITIONAL. The set holds one annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings-release exhibits, all dated on or before the cutoff and all issued by the registrant itself, which gives full statements, notes, debt and covenant descriptions, cash-flow supplements, adjusted EBITDA reconciliations and a post-quarter subsequent-events note. The limitations are the absence of executed financing documents and third-party material, the absence of a filed covenant calculation, and comparability breaks from reclassification and divestitures. The assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED.
### Source register

Each row records document family, original authority, entity and perimeter, period and basis, unit, and coverage. Authority: the filed 10-K and 10-Qs control financial-statement and note facts; the earnings releases are furnished exhibits whose figures are issuer statements supporting, never overriding, the filings. Identity and period are taken from the located content, not from file names.
| Alias | Family and authority | Entity and perimeter | Period and basis | Unit | Extraction coverage |

| 10-Q-Dec25 | Quarterly report, filed (original authority) | Open Text Corporation, consolidated | Three and six months ended December 31, 2025 (Q2 FY2026), unaudited; signed February 5, 2026 | USD thousands | 100 of 100 chunks retained, cover through signatures |

| 10-Q-Mar26 | Quarterly report, filed (original authority) | Open Text Corporation, consolidated | Three and nine months ended March 31, 2026 (Q3 FY2026), unaudited; signed May 7, 2026 | USD thousands | 105 of 105 chunks retained, cover through signatures |

| 10-Q-Sep26 | Quarterly report, filed (original authority) | Open Text Corporation, consolidated | Three months ended September 30, 2026 (Q1 FY2027), unaudited; signed November 5, 2026 | USD thousands | 90 of 90 chunks retained, cover through signatures and exhibit list |

| PR-May26 | Earnings release, exhibit 99.1 (issuer and management statements) | Open Text Corporation, consolidated | Q3 FY2026 and nine months, reported and non-GAAP | Headline in USD millions, tables in thousands | 28 of 28 chunks retained |

Identity evidence: the 10-Q for the latest quarter names the registrant on its cover [10-Q-Sep26 page:1 — "OPEN TEXT CORPORATION (Exact name of Registrant as specified in its charter)"] and the period [10-Q-Sep26 page:1 — "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026 OR"]. The annual report covers [10-K page:1 — "For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 OR"]. The two earlier 10-Qs cover [10-Q-Dec25 page:1 — "For the quarterly period ended December 31, 2025 OR"] and [10-Q-Mar26 page:1 — "For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026 OR"]. The releases are headed by quarter, for example [PR-Nov26 page:1 — "Fiscal 2027 First Quarter Highlights (in millions)(1)"], [PR-Aug26 page:1 — "Fiscal 2026 Fourth Quarter Highlights (in millions)(1)"] and [PR-May26 page:1 — "Fiscal 2026 Third Quarter Highlights (in millions)(1)"].
The latest 10-Q was signed on the cutoff date itself [10-Q-Sep26 page:90 — "Date: November 5, 2026"]. It is treated as inside the cutoff; the same applies to PR-Nov26.
### Version relationships and perimeter

- The filings are sequential periodic reports, not versions of one another. None supersedes another; each remains an active source for its own period. The 10-K covers the year to June 30, 2026, so the quarterly reports for Q2 and Q3 FY2026 are the only discrete-quarter filings for those quarters, and the Q4 FY2026 quarter appears as a discrete period only in PR-Aug26 and as a comparative in PR-Nov26.

- A Q1 FY2026 quarterly report and release were not supplied. The Q1 FY2026 figures exist only as the comparative column of 10-Q-Sep26 and PR-Nov26. No duplicate documents were found among the seven sources; overlapping facts (for example the Q3 FY2026 quarter in 10-Q-Mar26 and PR-May26) are different documents covering the same period, and the filing controls over the release.

- Entity roles: the registrant is the consolidated reporting entity and the only entity with supplied statements. Notes are issued by different group entities: the 2031 and 2030 senior notes by a subsidiary and guaranteed by the registrant [10-Q-Sep26 page:17 — "a subsidiary of the Company issued $650 million in aggregate principal amount of 4.125% senior notes due 2031 guaranteed by the Company"], and the annual report names that subsidiary [10-K page:117 — "OTHI merged with and into Open Text Inc. (OTI), a wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of the Company"]. The 2029 and 2028 senior notes were issued by the registrant itself [10-Q-Sep26 page:17 — "On November 24, 2021, the Company issued $850 million in aggregate principal amount of 3.875% senior notes due 2029"]. The secured instruments are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries [10-Q-Sep26 page:18 — "The Senior Secured Notes 2027 are guaranteed on a senior secured basis by certain of the Company’s subsidiaries"], and the term loan has subsidiary guarantors [10-Q-Sep26 page:21 — "The Acquisition Term Loan is unconditionally guaranteed by certain subsidiary guarantors, as defined in the Acquisition Term Loan"]. The identities of the guarantor group and any restricted or unrestricted split remain unresolved gaps (see Gaps).

- Perimeter changes inside the evidence window: the Vertica business was sold [10-Q-Sep26 page:38 — "On May 11, 2026, the Company completed the sale of its Vertica business to Rocket Software"] and the eDOCS business was sold [10-Q-Sep26 page:39 — "On January 12, 2026, the Company completed the sale of its eDOCS business to NetDocuments Software, Inc."]. Both are reported within income from operations until sale, not as discontinued operations, so FY2026 quarterly periods carry the divested results to different dates.
### Evidence by downstream demand
| Evidence demand | Located source evidence | Limitation carried forward |

### Conflicts and comparability breaks

1. Product-category restatement. The latest 10-Q reclassified categories and restated the comparative quarter [10-Q-Sep26 page:9 — "Prior period amounts have been reclassified to conform to the current period presentation."]. The bridge shows the prior presentation and the effect [10-Q-Sep26 page:9 — "Cybersecurity (Enterprise) 180,747 (71,410) 109,337"]. Earlier filings and releases therefore show product-category revenue on the old basis. Both bases are retained; neither controls the other. Downstream effect: product-category trends across PR-May26, PR-Aug26 and the latest quarter are not comparable without the bridge, and the bridge covers only the Q1 FY2026 quarter.

2. Net leverage. The only stated ratio is a management statement [PR-Nov26 page:3 — "Our net leverage ratio is 2.55x as of September 30, 2026."]. The covenant is defined differently in the filing (total debt less unrestricted cash, including guarantees and letters of credit, over trailing-twelve-month adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, restructuring, share-based compensation and other charges). The release does not state its definition or inputs. This is a definitional gap rather than a numerical conflict; it must not be presented as the covenant ratio. A management claim does not override the filing, which states only compliance.

3. Debt at the cutoff versus debt at period end. The balance sheet debt is as of September 30, 2026, while the same report records an October 2026 refinancing: [10-Q-Sep26 page:43 — "On October 1, 2026, the Company issued $500 million in aggregate principal amount of 6.70% senior secured notes due 2031"] and [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "On October 2, 2026, the Company purchased and cancelled $300.0 million of the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the Senior Notes 2028"]. The release states the same events [PR-Nov26 page:3 — "In October, OpenText completed a $1.0 billion senior secured notes offering"]. The documents are consistent with each other; the consequence is that two debt registers (period end and pro forma for the subsequent events) are needed and must be labelled.

4. Revolver maturity. The period-end filing describes the revolver as maturing in December 2028 and then records an amendment on October 1, 2026 extending it, subject to conditions [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "extend its maturity from December 19, 2028 to October 1, 2031, subject to certain conditions"]. Both are retained as dated facts.
5. Rounding. Release headlines are in millions and release tables in thousands; the filings are in thousands. Differences of that kind are rounding, not conflicts.
### Subsequent events and cutoff check

All seven sources are dated on or before the 2026-11-05 cutoff. Post-quarter facts in the latest report are subsequent events, kept separate from period-end balances. The dividend declared on November 3, 2026, with record date December 4, 2026 and payment date December 18, 2026, is a future contract term, labelled as such. The release also announces an investor day on February 10, 2027, a future event that is not evidence.

For the report's chart and model strip, the pack supplies discrete-quarter evidence for Q1 FY2027, Q3 FY2026 and Q2 FY2026 in the periodic reports and for Q4 FY2026 in the release; fiscal years FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024 for income and cash flow in the 10-K; add-back reconciliations; revenue by type and product category; instrument-level principal; cash-paid interest and tax; and business narrative. Gaps for that use: facility-level carrying values, covenant EBITDA, and a Q1 FY2026 original filing. The assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. No normalized quarters, reconciliation or input acceptance is asserted.
## Calculations

No new calculation is performed in CP-0. Figures shown above are quoted from the sources inside citations, unchanged, and none is derived. The only counts are coverage counts: 311 of 311 chunks for the annual report, 100 of 100, 105 of 105 and 90 of 90 for the three quarterly reports, and 28 of 28, 31 of 31 and 20 of 20 for the three releases, which is 685 of 685 chunks. A chunk count establishes extraction completeness only; it is not a readiness proxy and does not show fidelity.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Interest burden and leverage have fallen, cash generation is solid and covenant headroom is wide, but revenue is shrinking and the October 2026 refinancing replaced cheaper notes with higher-coupon secured debt. | Medium | Covenant earnings, letters of credit and post-refinancing cash are not supplied, so headroom and liquidity after October 2026 cannot be fully measured. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Reported covenant leverage fell each quarter from December 2025 to June 2026 against a maximum of 4.50. | Wide headroom to the maintenance test, though the September 2026 value is only attributed to management. | Medium |
| Revenue fell in the latest quarter while the adjusted EBITDA margin was 35.8 percent. | Profit is being defended through cost actions while client support and license revenue decline. | Medium |

| October 2026 secured notes replaced the 2027 secured notes, and part of the 2028 notes was bought back. | The nearest large maturity is extended, but secured debt rises and the cash cost of the exchange is not supplied. | Medium |
### Financial base view

For OPEN TEXT CORP the financial base shows a credit that has de-levered and cut interest cost while its top line contracts. Gross debt principal at June 30, 2026 was below June 30, 2025 by the amount of repayments in FY2026, funded by divestiture proceeds and cash on hand, and debt at September 30, 2026 was almost unchanged from June 30, 2026. Against adjusted EBITDA, total debt fell from 3.63x at FY2025 to 3.07x at FY2026 and was 3.10x on a last-twelve-months basis at September 30, 2026; EBITDA to cash interest paid rose from 3.69x in FY2024 to 5.92x in FY2026 and 6.26x on the last-twelve-months basis. The calculated covenant ratio printed in the filings fell from 3.35 at December 31, 2025 to 2.75 at June 30, 2026 against a 4.50 maximum, so maintenance headroom is large on the printed figures. The pressure points are the contracting revenue base (Q1 FY2027 revenue down year on year, with client support and license lines falling while cloud grew), the divestitures that removed earnings together with debt, the heavy shareholder distributions in FY2026 relative to free cash flow, an unquantified Canada Revenue Agency tax dispute, and the October 2026 refinancing that lengthened maturities but swapped 6.90% secured notes due 2027 for 6.70% and 7.15% secured notes due 2031 and 2033, raising the secured debt share. The view is bounded by three missing inputs: covenant EBITDA, letters of credit that may reduce revolver availability, and cash after the October 2026 transactions.

| Acquisition Term Loan | Borrower not named in the notes; unconditionally guaranteed by certain subsidiary guarantors | Floating, Term SOFR plus 1.75%; 5.44% at Sep 30, 2026; seven-year term from funding | 1,527,563 | 1,527,563 | First charge on substantially all assets, pari passu with revolver |

| Revolver (750,000 commitment) | Borrowers not named in the notes | Term SOFR plus 1.25% to 1.75%; matures December 19, 2028, extended on October 1, 2026 to October 1, 2031 subject to conditions | 0 | 0 | First charge, pari passu |

Evidence for the register: [10-Q-Sep26 page:16 — "Senior Secured Notes 2027 1,000,000 1,000,000"], [10-Q-Sep26 page:16 — "Acquisition Term Loan 1,527,563 1,536,525"], [10-Q-Sep26 page:19 — "On October 1, 2026, the Company issued $500 million in aggregate principal amount of 6.70% senior secured notes due 2031"], [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "On October 2, 2026, the Company purchased and cancelled $300.0 million of the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the Senior Notes 2028"], [10-Q-Sep26 page:20 — "applicable margin of 1.75%"], [10-K page:120 — "Senior Notes 2030 are guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by the Company"] and [10-Q-Sep26 page:18 — "Senior Secured Notes 2027 bear interest at a rate of 6.90% per annum"].

Secured and unsecured split after October 2, 2026 (calculated): secured principal is the term loan 1,527,563 plus new secured notes 500,000 plus 500,000, which is 2,527,563 of 5,527,563 total, or 45.7 percent; before the transactions secured principal was 1,527,563 plus 1,000,000, or 2,527,563 of 5,827,563, or 43.4 percent. The unsecured notes fall from 3,300,000 to 3,000,000. Secured debt in absolute terms is unchanged; its share rises because unsecured notes were bought back. The revolver, if drawn, would rank with the secured debt.

Annual cash coupon change on the exchanged notes (calculated): new notes 500,000 at 6.70% plus 500,000 at 7.15% is 69,250; redeemed 1,000,000 at 6.90% is 69,000; tendered 300,000 at 3.875% is 11,625; the net change is a reduction of 11,375 per year before premium, fees and the lost interest income on cash used. The redemption premium and the tender price are not printed as amounts.
### Covenants and liquidity

The revolver and the term loan both carry a maintenance test [10-Q-Sep26 page:19 — "we must maintain a “consolidated net leverage” ratio of no more than 4.50:1.00 at the end of each financial quarter"]. The ratio is defined with debt reduced by unrestricted cash, including guarantees and letters of credit, over trailing twelve months earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, restructuring, share-based compensation and other miscellaneous charges. The printed values are: [10-Q-Dec25 page:23 — "as calculated in accordance with the applicable agreement, was 3.35:1:00"], [10-Q-Mar26 page:24 — "as calculated in accordance with the applicable agreement, was 3.02:1:00"] and [10-K page:124 — "as calculated in accordance with the applicable agreement, was 2.75:1.00"]. For September 30, 2026 the 10-Q states [10-Q-Sep26 page:21 — "As of September 30, 2026, we are in compliance with our consolidated net leverage ratio covenant."] and the earnings release gives a management statement [PR-Nov26 page:3 — "Our net leverage ratio is 2.55x as of September 30, 2026."] with no definition or inputs.

Headroom to the 4.50 maximum on the printed ratios (calculated, in turns of leverage): 1.15 at December 31, 2025, 1.48 at March 31, 2026 and 1.75 at June 30, 2026. The covenant ratio is higher than the simple net debt to adjusted EBITDA computed above (2.75 against 2.56 at June 30, 2026). The definition differs from the metric computed here: it adds guarantees and letters of credit to debt, whose amounts are not supplied, and uses covenant EBITDA, which is not printed; the gap cannot be reconciled from the pack. A second leverage test governs incremental term debt capacity [10-Q-Sep26 page:20 — "additional amounts, subject to meeting a “consolidated senior secured net leverage” ratio not exceeding 2.75:1.00"].

Liquidity at September 30, 2026 (calculated): cash and cash equivalents 983,292 plus the undrawn 750,000 revolver is 1,733,292 before any letters of credit drawn on the revolver. Letters of credit and bank guarantees are described only generically [10-Q-Sep26 page:29 — "guarantees relating to taxes and letters of credit on behalf of parties with whom we conduct business"]; a search of the pack for letters of credit, standby, bank guarantee and revolver availability wording found no amount. The same total at June 30, 2026 was 956,024 plus 750,000, or 1,706,024. Near-term maturities: the current portion of term-loan amortization is 35,850 and the first note maturity was December 1, 2027 until the October 2026 redemption. The revolver matured December 19, 2028 at the balance-sheet date and was extended on October 1, 2026, and the first note maturity after the October 2026 redemption is February 15, 2028. The term loan maturity date is not printed, but the contractual-obligation table shows only 254,245 (principal plus interest) falling due between October 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027, which is consistent with no term loan balloon within twelve months. Cash after October 2026 is Not supplied; the transactions used cash on hand [10-Q-Sep26 page:18 — "together with cash on hand, to fund the purchase and cancellation of $300.0 million"], so cash fell by an amount that is not supplied and pro forma liquidity is lower than the September figure.
### Cash flow quality and distributions

Operating cash flow was 1,006,817 in FY2026 against adjusted EBITDA of 1,903,162, and free cash flow was 807,517 (issuer definition). Cash taxes (300,062) and cash interest (321,694) are two of the larger cash claims between EBITDA and operating cash flow, together 621,756. Working capital moved against cash: contract assets absorbed 147,700 in FY2026 and receivables days sales outstanding rose to 48 days in Q1 FY2027 from 41 days a year earlier [10-Q-Sep26 page:79 — "a days sales outstanding (DSO) of 48 days, compared to our DSO of 41 days"]. In FY2026 the company paid dividends of 268,357, repurchased shares for 416,411 and purchased treasury stock for 52,901 [10-K page:236 — "Payments of dividends to shareholders (268,357) (271,523) (267,362)"], a total of 737,669, which is 91.4 percent of free cash flow (calculated). In Q1 FY2027 dividends of $66.5 million and repurchases of $23.4 million were paid or made [10-Q-Sep26 page:80 — "in the aggregate amount of $66.5 million"], about 89.9 million against free cash flow of 138.5 million. A further dividend of $0.28 per share was declared on November 3, 2026, payable December 18, 2026, a future term. Debt repayment in FY2026 was 648,852 in the cash flow statement, which equals the fall in principal (6,485,375 less 5,836,525 is 648,850; the difference of 2 is not explained in the pack).
### Claims outside the debt figure

- Canada Revenue Agency dispute: potential liability for fiscal 2012 to 2016 limited to penalties, interest and provincial taxes of approximately $88.8 million, with approximately $32.0 million provisionally paid [10-Q-Sep26 page:30 — "approximately $88.8 million"]; for fiscal 2017 to 2021 an adverse outcome could reduce deferred tax assets by up to approximately $470 million [10-Q-Sep26 page:85 — "of up to approximately $470 million"], with a cash tax effect over several years and no accrual recorded. Outside the debt figure and not in net debt.

- Net pension liability of 98,914 on the balance sheet, with plans outside Canada and the United States, mainly Germany [10-Q-Sep26 page:2 — "Pension liability, net (Note 10) 98,914 100,473"]. Outside debt.

- Leases: operating lease liabilities of 64,822 current and 137,939 long-term on the balance sheet [10-Q-Sep26 page:2 — "Long-term operating lease liabilities (Note 4) 137,939 138,425"], undiscounted operating lease payments of 227,773 and finance lease obligations of 309 [10-Q-Sep26 page:83 — "Finance lease obligations (3) 309 309"]. Outside the debt figure.

- Purchase obligations of 246,133 and future leases not yet commenced of 53,544 [10-Q-Sep26 page:83 — "Purchase obligations for contracts not accounted for as lease obligations 246,133"]. Outside debt.

- Restructuring: the Business Optimization Plan had incurred 246.2 million of up to approximately 270.0 million of expected costs at September 30, 2026 [10-Q-Sep26 page:55 — "we have incurred $246.2 million of the total expected costs of up to approximately $270.0 million"]. Special charges were 33,290 in Q1 FY2027.
- Factoring, supply-chain finance, consent decrees: a search found no such arrangement in the pack; nothing is recorded.
### Subsequent events

All dated October 1 and 2, 2026 and November 3, 2026, after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and inside the cutoff: the secured notes issue, the redemption of the 2027 secured notes, the 2028 notes tender, the revolver amendment and the dividend declaration [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "extend its maturity from December 19, 2028 to October 1, 2031, subject to certain conditions"]. The earlier divestitures (eDOCS sold January 12, 2026 and Vertica May 11, 2026) funded 313.0 million of prepayments of the term loan and reduced revenue and EBITDA from those dates; FY2026 and Q1 FY2026 include their results to sale, while Q1 FY2027 does not.
### Comparability and definition limits

Product-category revenue was restated in Q1 FY2027, so category trends before that quarter are not comparable without the bridge (limited to Q1 FY2026). Release headline figures are in millions and rounded; filings are in thousands. Adjusted EBITDA includes add-backs for share-based compensation and special charges (33,290 in Q1 FY2027 and 133,020 in FY2026), so it is higher than reported operating profit plus depreciation and amortization alone; special charges recur each year (135,305 in FY2024, 145,890 in FY2025, 133,020 in FY2026), which weakens the case for treating them as one-off. Cash interest paid is gross of interest received.
## Calculations
All inputs are in US$ thousands as printed; ratios are rounded to two decimals.

1. LTM adjusted EBITDA at September 30, 2026 = FY2026 1,903,162 minus Q1 FY2026 467,411 plus Q1 FY2027 442,432 = 1,878,183. Inputs: [10-K page:136 — "Adjusted EBITDA $ 1,903,162"], [10-Q-Sep26 page:78 — "Adjusted EBITDA $ 467,411"], [10-Q-Sep26 page:76 — "Adjusted EBITDA $ 442,432"].

2. LTM adjusted EBITDA at December 31, 2025 = FY2025 1,784,465 minus six months FY2025 945,285 plus six months FY2026 958,597 = 1,797,777. Inputs: [10-Q-Dec25 page:88 — "Adjusted EBITDA $ 945,285"], [10-Q-Dec25 page:85 — "Adjusted EBITDA $ 958,597"], [10-K page:139 — "Adjusted EBITDA $ 1,784,465"].

3. LTM adjusted EBITDA at March 31, 2026 = 1,784,465 minus nine months FY2025 1,340,536 plus nine months FY2026 1,396,511 = 1,840,440. Inputs: [10-Q-Mar26 page:93 — "Adjusted EBITDA $ 1,340,536"], [10-Q-Mar26 page:90 — "Adjusted EBITDA $ 1,396,511"].

5. Net debt (principal less cash and cash equivalents): FY2025 6,485,375 less 1,156,496 = 5,328,879 (2.99x); December 2025 6,467,450 less 1,271,374 = 5,196,076 (2.89x); March 2026 6,295,488 less 1,254,144 = 5,041,344 (2.74x); FY2026 5,836,525 less 956,024 = 4,880,501 (2.56x); September 2026 5,827,563 less 983,292 = 4,844,271 (2.58x). Cash inputs: [10-K page:233 — "Cash and cash equivalents $ 956,024 $ 1,156,496"], [10-Q-Dec25 page:2 — "Cash and cash equivalents $ 1,271,374 $ 1,156,496"], [10-Q-Mar26 page:2 — "Cash and cash equivalents $ 1,254,144 $ 1,156,496"], [10-Q-Sep26 page:2 — "Cash and cash equivalents $ 983,292 $ 956,024"].

6. Interest cover = adjusted EBITDA / cash paid for interest: FY2024 1,970,200 / 533,866 = 3.69; FY2025 1,784,465 / 352,383 = 5.06; FY2026 1,903,162 / 321,694 = 5.92; LTM cash interest 321,694 minus 79,500 plus 57,917 = 300,111, and 1,878,183 / 300,111 = 6.26; Q1 FY2026 467,411 / 79,500 = 5.88 and Q1 FY2027 442,432 / 57,917 = 7.64. Inputs: [10-K page:306 — "Cash paid during the period for interest $ 321,694 $ 352,383 $ 533,866"], [10-Q-Sep26 page:42 — "Cash paid during the period for interest $ 57,917 $ 79,500"].

7. LTM revenue = 5,246,401 minus 1,288,135 plus 1,236,634 = 5,194,900; LTM operating income = 1,082,597 minus 269,949 plus 250,811 = 1,063,459; LTM net income attributable = 643,022 minus 146,616 plus 155,247 = 651,653; LTM operating cash flow = 1,006,817 minus 147,763 plus 172,273 = 1,031,327; LTM capex = 199,300 minus 46,534 plus 33,756 = 186,522; LTM free cash flow = 1,031,327 minus 186,522 = 844,805; LTM cash taxes = 300,062 minus 77,321 plus 82,200 = 304,941. Inputs: [10-K page:234 — "Total revenues 5,246,401 5,168,405 5,769,577"], [10-Q-Sep26 page:3 — "Total revenues 1,236,634 1,288,135"], [10-K page:236 — "Net cash provided by operating activities 1,006,817 830,618 967,691"], [PR-Nov26 page:16 — "GAAP-based cash flows provided by operating activities $ 172,273"], [PR-Nov26 page:20 — "GAAP-based cash flows provided by operating activities $ 147,763"].

8. Revenue growth: FY2026 5,246,401 / 5,168,405 minus 1 = 1.5 percent; FY2025 5,168,405 / 5,769,577 minus 1 = minus 10.4 percent; Q1 FY2027 1,236,634 / 1,288,135 minus 1 = minus 4.0 percent, which matches the release [PR-Nov26 page:2 — "Total revenues $ 1,237 $ 1,288 $ (52) (4.0) %"].
9. Margins = adjusted EBITDA / revenue: FY2024 34.1, FY2025 34.5, FY2026 36.3, Q1 FY2026 36.3, Q1 FY2027 35.8, LTM 36.2 percent.

10. Free cash flow = operating cash flow minus additions of property and equipment: FY2024 967,691 minus 159,295 = 808,396; FY2025 830,618 minus 143,222 = 687,396; FY2026 1,006,817 minus 199,300 = 807,517; Q1 FY2026 147,763 minus 46,534 = 101,229; Q1 FY2027 172,273 minus 33,756 = 138,517. These match the issuer's reconciliations [PR-Nov26 page:16 — "Free cash flow $ 138,517"] and [PR-Aug26 page:23 — "Free cash flow $ 807,517"].
11. Covenant headroom = 4.50 minus printed ratio: 1.15, 1.48, 1.75.

13. Secured share, coupon change and distributions as set out in their sections: 2,527,563 / 5,527,563 = 45.7 percent; 2,527,563 / 5,827,563 = 43.4 percent; 737,669 / 807,517 = 91.4 percent; coupon 69,250 minus 69,000 minus 11,625 = minus 11,375.

Quarterly adjusted EBITDA ties: 467,411 + 491,186 + 437,914 + 506,651 = 1,903,162, equal to the FY2026 figure. Inputs: [10-Q-Dec25 page:79 — "Adjusted EBITDA $ 491,186"], [10-Q-Mar26 page:84 — "Adjusted EBITDA $ 437,914"], [PR-Aug26 page:21 — "Adjusted EBITDA $ 506,651"].
## Gaps
| Gap | Effect | Action |

| Covenant EBITDA and the guarantee and letter-of-credit amounts in the covenant debt definition are not printed; the September 30, 2026 covenant ratio is not printed (management figure only) | Headroom at September 2026 cannot be filed-fact; computed leverage does not reconcile to the printed covenant ratio | Treat 2.55 as attributed; use printed values for earlier dates; obtain the compliance certificate if needed |
| Letters of credit drawn on the revolver, and any other facility usage, are Not supplied | Undrawn availability is an upper bound | State availability as undrawn commitment only |

| Cash after the October 2026 transactions, the tender price and the redemption premium are Not supplied | Pro forma net debt and liquidity cannot be computed | Await the next filing; label pro forma metrics as principal only |

| Acquisition Term Loan maturity date and quarterly payment dates are not printed | Maturity chart cannot place the term loan balloon in a fiscal year | Use the contractual-obligation buckets as an outer bound |
| June 30, 2024 debt and the revolver balance are not in the pack | FY2024 leverage and liquidity are Not supplied | Obtain the FY2025 10-K if a three-year leverage trend is needed |

| Guarantor and non-guarantor financial information, ratings and executed financing documents are not supplied | Structural subordination and recovery cannot be assessed here | Carry to later modules as not assessable |
| Adjusted EBITDA is an issuer-defined non-GAAP measure and its add-backs recur | Leverage and cover based on it are favourable to the GAAP view | Show GAAP income from operations alongside |
| Q1 FY2026 original quarterly filing and balance sheet not in the pack | Q1 FY2026 balance-sheet metrics Not supplied | Use the comparative columns only |
## Next module

Pass to CP-1A (business and transaction context) and then CP-2 (credit synthesis). CP-2 should carry these items: period-end and pro forma debt kept separate; the printed covenant ratios (3.35, 3.02, 2.75 against 4.50) separate from the management 2.55 and from the computed net leverage; interest cover and leverage on issuer-defined adjusted EBITDA; the unquantified letters of credit and post-October cash; the revenue decline in client support and license against cloud growth; the high share of free cash flow returned to shareholders; and the Canada Revenue Agency exposure outside debt.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| A listed, widely held software company with no sponsor, recurring revenue of 84.1 percent of the latest quarter, a new chief executive and revenue down in the latest quarter; the October 2026 refinancing extended maturities at higher coupons. | Medium | Only management and filing narrative is available: no customer data, ratings, executed debt documents or third-party view. |

### Business and transaction view

For OPEN TEXT CORP the business is a diversified, global enterprise software and cybersecurity vendor whose revenue is dominated by annual-renewal client support and cloud subscriptions, which gives good revenue visibility but a base that fell in the latest quarter, with the support and license lines declining and growth concentrated in cloud lines. The registrant is a widely held listed company with no sponsor and no holder above about eleven percent, so the creditor risk is not sponsor extraction; it is a management and Board capital allocation choice between debt reduction, a quarterly dividend and share repurchases, taken in a year of leadership change and a strategic enterprise assessment whose conclusions are scheduled for an investor day in February 2027. The credit-relevant history is acquisition-led: the 2023 Micro Focus acquisition created the debt load, the 2024 AMC sale and the 2026 eDOCS and Vertica sales repaid part of it at the cost of earnings, and the October 2026 refinancing replaced the 2027 secured notes and part of the 2028 notes with secured notes due 2031 and 2033, which extends the maturity wall but raises the share of secured debt and the coupon on the replaced paper. Management's FY2027 outlook, a management statement, points to a lower margin and lower free cash flow than the last twelve months, which is the main forward uncertainty. Evidence is primary and dated for facts and management-only for outlook and strategy; no customer-level, rating or executed-document evidence is available.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The transaction that matters for the creditor is the October 2026 refinancing, a closed subsequent event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and inside the cutoff. Type: a refinancing and partial liability management. Parties: the registrant as issuer, guaranteed on a senior secured basis by certain subsidiaries; the initial purchasers, trustees and holders tendering are not named in the pack. Sponsor: none. On October 1, 2026 the company issued two series of senior secured notes: [10-Q-Sep26 page:43 — "On October 1, 2026, the Company issued $500 million in aggregate principal amount of 6.70% senior secured notes due 2031"] and a second 500 million series at 7.15 percent due 2033, both paying interest semi-annually from April 15, 2027 and maturing on October 15, 2031 and October 15, 2033 respectively. Debt raised is therefore 1,000 million of new secured notes, secured with the same priority as the senior credit facilities [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "are secured with the same priority as the Company’s senior credit facilities"] and structurally subordinated to liabilities of subsidiaries that do not guarantee them. Use of proceeds: on October 2, 2026 the proceeds, together with cash on hand, funded the redemption in full of the 1.0 billion 6.90 percent senior secured notes due 2027 including the redemption premium, accrued interest and costs, and the cash purchase and cancellation of 300.0 million of the 3.875 percent senior notes due 2028 [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "On October 2, 2026, the Company purchased and cancelled $300.0 million of the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the Senior Notes 2028"]. The revolving credit facility of 750.0 million, undrawn at September 30, 2026, was amended on October 1, 2026 to extend its maturity from December 19, 2028 to October 1, 2031, subject to certain conditions, and its borrowings rank pari passu with the term loan and the new secured notes.

Effect on the credit, as the financial base handoff computes it: principal debt falls from 5,827,563 to 5,527,563 (US$ thousands); the nearest note maturity moves from December 1, 2027 to February 15, 2028 and falls from 1,900,000 across the two near notes to 600,000 for the remaining 2028 notes; new maturities of 500,000 fall in fiscal 2032 and 500,000 in fiscal 2034; secured principal stays at 2,527,563 while its share of the total rises from 43.4 percent to 45.7 percent; and the annual cash coupon on the exchanged notes falls by 11,375 before premium and fees. The cost side is not quantified in the pack: the redemption premium, the tender price and the cash used are not stated, so the liquidity effect is a reduction of cash on hand by an amount that is not supplied. The management characterisation is that the transactions provide greater financial flexibility [PR-Nov26 page:1 — "providing the Company with greater financial flexibility"], which is Management Language and is not adopted; the documented facts are a longer maturity profile, a higher secured share and coupons of 6.70 and 7.15 percent against 6.90 percent on the retired secured notes. Status: closed. New debt issues in the pack: only these two series; there are no pending or committed financings, no acquisition financing and no dividend recapitalisation.

Earlier transactions that shape the structure: the 2023 Micro Focus acquisition for 6.2 billion, for which the term loan and the 2027 secured notes were raised; the 2024 AMC sale for 2.275 billion, which funded a term loan prepayment of 1.31 billion in FY2024 together with cash on hand; and the eDOCS and Vertica sales in FY2026 for 163.0 million and 150.0 million, each applied to prepay the term loan. These sales removed revenue and earnings while reducing debt, which is why the divestiture comparability break is carried in every period comparison. A further dividend of $0.28 per share was declared on November 3, 2026, payable December 18, 2026; it is a future term, not an executed payment.
### Ownership, control and capital allocation

Ownership is dispersed and institutional: the largest holder is just over eleven percent and directors and executive officers hold about two and a half percent. No sponsor, no prior sponsor ownership and no dividend recapitalisation history appears in the pack; none of the ownership percentages is inferred beyond the table. Capital allocation is documented: the company declares a quarterly non-cumulative dividend (dividends declared of $1.00, $1.05 and $1.10 per share in FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 per the equity statement [10-K page:236 — "Dividends declared ($1.10 per Common Share)"]) and runs a repurchase programme renewed in August 2026 [10-Q-Sep26 page:82 — "the Company renewed its share repurchase plan"]. The financial base handoff shows that shareholder distributions in FY2026 were 91.4 percent of free cash flow, in the same year that debt principal fell by 648,850. The dividend is subject to contractual limits [10-K page:67 — "Our dividend payments are subject to relevant contractual limitations, including those in our existing credit agreements"], whose terms are not in the pack, so legal capacity for distributions cannot be measured here.

| Theme | Evidence | Risk mechanic | Credit implication |

| Revenue durability | Recurring revenue is 84.1 percent of Q1 FY2027 revenue; support is falling and cloud renewal rate eased to 95 percent | Annual renewals give visibility, but support attrition and slower cloud migration reduce the contracted base that services interest | Leverage tolerance depends on holding recurring revenue; monitor renewal rate and support trend |

Both are retained and neither is reconciled here. The financial statement note is the filed financial authority for the balance at June 30, 2026, so the debt register uses the note; the risk factor figure is unexplained in the pack. Effect: the size of the term loan should be taken only from the notes and balance sheet.

2. eDOCS product category. The annual report places the business in one category [10-K page:19 — "eDOCS business (eDOCS), a part of our Analytics product category"] while the latest quarterly report places it in another [10-Q-Sep26 page:52 — "an on-premise solution (eDOCS), a part of its Portfolio product category"]. Both versions are retained; the later basis applies to Q1 FY2027 and its comparative only. Effect: category trends across filings are not comparable.

| Consumer | Readiness | What to take from this module | Why it matters | Gap | Required action |

| CP-2 (credit synthesis) | Ready with limitations | Business risk rows, ownership and sponsor facts, governance behaviours, credit translations, conflicts | Business risk is one of its drivers | Customer concentration, ratings, executed documents, guarantor structure not supplied | Carry limitations, label outlook as management language, state no sponsor |

## Calculations

1. Recurring share of Q1 FY2027 revenue = (cloud 505,469 + client support 534,111) / total revenues 1,236,634 = 1,039,580 / 1,236,634 = 84.1 percent. Inputs: [10-Q-Sep26 page:3 — "Cloud services and subscriptions $ 505,469 $ 484,509"], [10-Q-Sep26 page:3 — "Client support 534,111 586,845"], [10-Q-Sep26 page:3 — "Total revenues 1,236,634 1,288,135"].

2. FY2027 outlook-implied adjusted EBITDA: low = revenue 5,135 million x 32 percent = 1,643.2 million; high = revenue 5,185 million x 33 percent = 1,711.1 million. Compared with last twelve months adjusted EBITDA of 1,878,183 thousand (financial base handoff), the range is about 167 to 235 million lower. Inputs: [10-Q-Sep26 page:53 — "Total revenues (as reported) (in millions) (1) $5,135 to $5,185"].

5. Secured share after October 2026 and distributions share of free cash flow are taken from the financial base handoff (45.7 percent and 91.4 percent) without recalculation; inputs 2,527,563 / 5,527,563 and 737,669 / 807,517.

6. The Q1 FY2027 recurring revenue is described by the issuer as 1,039.6 million [10-Q-Sep26 page:50 — "was $1,039.6 million, down 3.0% compared to the same period in the prior fiscal year"], consistent with calculation 1.

| Canada Revenue Agency matter amount and timing remain uncertain | Documentary Fact with open outcome, medium | CP-2 | Treat as a contingent claim outside debt |
## Next module

Pass to CP-2 (credit synthesis) with: no sponsor and dispersed ownership; recurring revenue share and its declining support line; the FY2027 outlook as management language below the last twelve months; the leadership change and strategic review as governance uncertainties; the October 2026 refinancing as a maturity extension with higher secured debt; and the two logged conflicts. spans.text: ## Request

OPEN TEXT CORP (registrant Open Text Corporation, consolidated, USD), as of 2026-11-05, credit_snapshot pathway: a fundamental credit synthesis built only on the accepted source readiness, financial base and business and transaction context handoffs, covering business risk, financial risk, liquidity and the gaps that limit them. Fiscal year ends June 30; Q1 FY2027 is the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
## Sources
### Issuer sources behind the upstream handoffs

Run context (not issuer evidence): sha256 cdf3e7e5d139751591ad9d995cdcdd0bad8e54e428f889bfd4cbcc1eae58ab70. This synthesis quotes no source text; every claim rests on the handoffs below, and the filings were re-opened only to confirm the inherited correction on the covenant ratio.
### Supplied handoffs

| CP-0 | readiness | ae7b653c84c72f696d77e449940280b63c6a90d2bec9f8b7dc52fb0396bbbec0 |
